en: Many people have said that this app is very useful.
tamil: இந்த ஆப் ரொம்ப பயனுள்ளதுன்னு நிறைய பேர் சொல்லியிருக்காங்க.
explain: 'Have said' is used when something was said before and it still matters now.
usage: Use it when you suggest a good app or tool to a friend or a colleague.
leelaQ: Which app do you find very useful?
answer: I find a map app very useful because I travel a lot.

en: Did you like the movie as much as I did?
tamil: நான் ரசிச்ச அளவுக்கு நீங்களும் படத்தை ரசிச்சீங்களா?
explain: 'As much as' compares two equal things.
usage: Ask it right after you watch a film together.
leelaQ: What was the last movie you really liked?
answer: I really liked a comedy film because it made everyone laugh.

en: You have made a good choice with this laptop.
tamil: இந்த லேப்டாப் நீங்க நல்லா தேர்ந்தெடுத்திருக்கீங்க.
explain: 'Have made a good choice' praises something the person has just done.
usage: Say it when a friend or a customer shows you something new they bought.
leelaQ: What was your best purchase this year?
answer: My best purchase was a pair of good shoes for walking.

en: I would rather stay at home on Sunday.
tamil: ஞாயிற்றுக்கிழமை நான் வீட்லயே இருக்கத்தான் விரும்புவேன்.
explain: 'Would rather' + verb means you prefer one thing over another.
usage: Use it when friends plan an outing and you want a quiet day.
leelaQ: What would you rather do on a free Sunday?
answer: I would rather sleep late and watch a movie on a free Sunday.

en: Could you share your opinion on this draft?
tamil: இந்த டிராஃப்ட் பத்தி உங்க கருத்தை சொல்ல முடியுமா?
explain: 'Share your opinion' is a formal and polite phrase for feedback.
usage: Use it at work when you send a document or an email for review.
leelaQ: Who do you ask for feedback on your work?
answer: I ask my senior colleague because she gives clear suggestions.

en: This song is nicer than the old one.
tamil: இந்த பாட்டு பழசை விட அழகா இருக்கு.
explain: 'Nicer than' compares two things. We use 'than' after a comparative.
usage: Use it in a friendly chat about music or films.
leelaQ: What kind of songs do you enjoy most?
answer: I enjoy melody songs because they make me feel calm.

en: I will never choose cheap quality over safety.
tamil: நான் பாதுகாப்பை விட்டுட்டு மலிவான தரத்தை எப்பவும் தேர்ந்தெடுக்க மாட்டேன்.
explain: 'Never' is a strong negative word. 'Will never' shows a firm decision.
usage: Use it when you talk about helmets, electrical items or children's products.
leelaQ: What is one thing you will never compromise on?
answer: I will never compromise on safety when I buy a helmet.

en: Our team did a great job this month.
tamil: இந்த மாசம் நம்ம டீம் சூப்பரா வேலை செஞ்சாங்க.
explain: 'Did a great job' is a common phrase for praise at work.
usage: Say it to colleagues or your manager at the end of a busy month.
leelaQ: What was the last great job you did at work or school?
answer: I finished my project on time, and my teacher was very happy.

en: Why did you choose this college?
tamil: நீங்க ஏன் இந்த காலேஜை தேர்ந்தெடுத்தீங்க?
context: Asking a reason for a choice.
explain: 'Why did you choose...?' asks for the reason behind a past decision.
usage: Use it when you meet a new classmate or a junior student.
leelaQ: Why did you choose your school or college?
answer: I chose it because it was near my house and had good teachers.

en: I am going to vote for the second plan.
tamil: நான் ரெண்டாவது திட்டத்துக்கு தான் ஓட்டு போடப் போறேன்.
context: Saying which plan you will support.
explain: 'Going to' shows a decision you have already made.
usage: Use it in a group decision, such as a college club or a housing society meeting.
leelaQ: How do you decide when you vote for something?
answer: I read about each choice and then I vote for the best one.

en: Compared to Bangalore, Coimbatore is calmer and cleaner.
tamil: பெங்களூரோட ஒப்பிட்டா கோயம்புத்தூர் அமைதியாவும் சுத்தமாவும் இருக்கு.
explain: 'Compared to' starts a comparison. 'Calmer' and 'cleaner' are comparatives.
usage: Use it when you tell friends about two cities you know.
leelaQ: Which city do you find calmer, and why?
answer: I find my small town calmer because there is less traffic.

en: Have you tried both shops to compare their prices?
tamil: விலையை ஒப்பிட நீங்க ரெண்டு கடையிலயும் பார்த்தீங்களா?
explain: 'Have you tried...?' asks about an experience up to now.
usage: Ask it when a friend complains about a high price.
leelaQ: Do you compare prices before you buy things?
answer: Yes, I compare prices in two shops before I buy something big.

en: That is exactly what I was thinking.
tamil: நானும் சரியா அதே தான் யோசிச்சுட்டு இருந்தேன்.
explain: 'Exactly' shows full agreement. 'Was thinking' is a past continuous feeling.
usage: Say it when a friend says the same thing you had in mind.
leelaQ: When did a friend say exactly what you were thinking?
answer: My friend said we should go home early, and I was thinking the same.

en: Try the new route tomorrow, it is much faster.
tamil: நாளைக்கு புது ரூட்ல போய் பாருங்க, அது ரொம்ப வேகம்.
explain: A command with a reason sounds friendly: 'Try this, it is faster.'
usage: Say it to a friend or a driver who is stuck in daily traffic.
leelaQ: What is the fastest way to reach your office or college?
answer: The fastest way is the bypass road, but the metro is also quick.

en: The main reason I like walking is that it is free.
tamil: நான் நடக்கிறது பிடிக்க முக்கிய காரணம், அது இலவசம்.
context: Giving the main reason for a habit.
explain: 'The main reason is that...' gives a clear reason in one sentence.
usage: Use it when someone asks why you walk or cycle to work.
leelaQ: What is the main reason you like your favourite hobby?
answer: The main reason I like cycling is that it keeps me fit.

en: Both options are fine, but I lean towards the cheaper one.
tamil: ரெண்டு ஆப்ஷனும் நல்லது தான், ஆனா நான் விலை குறைவானது பக்கம் சாயுறேன்.
explain: 'Lean towards' means you slightly prefer one choice.
usage: Use it when you must pick between two good choices and the price decides it.
leelaQ: What helps you decide between two good choices?
answer: The price and the quality help me decide between two choices.

en: Which is more useful for students, a tablet or a laptop?
tamil: மாணவர்களுக்கு டேப்லெட்டா, லேப்டாப்பா எது அதிக பயனுள்ளது?
context: Asking for advice on a device.
explain: 'More useful' compares two things. 'Which' is for a small set of choices.
usage: Ask it when you help a student or a parent choose a gadget.
leelaQ: What device do you use most for studying or work?
answer: I use my laptop most because it is easy for typing.

en: I was wrong earlier, your idea is better.
tamil: நான் முன்னாடி தப்பா சொல்லிட்டேன், உங்க ஐடியா தான் நல்லது.
context: Accepting that someone else was right.
explain: Saying 'I was wrong' with a calm voice shows maturity and respect.
usage: Use it at work or at home when you change your mind after a discussion.
leelaQ: Have you ever changed your mind after hearing someone's idea?
answer: Yes, I changed my mind when my friend explained his plan clearly.

en: I do not like spicy food as much as you do.
tamil: உங்களை மாதிரி எனக்கு காரமான சாப்பாடு அவ்வளவா பிடிக்காது.
explain: 'Not as much as' compares two people when one likes something less.
usage: Use it at a restaurant or a family lunch when your taste is different.
leelaQ: How spicy do you like your food?
answer: I like medium spicy food, not too hot.

en: I think we should ask the manager before deciding.
tamil: முடிவு எடுக்கிறதுக்கு முன்னாடி மேனேஜர்கிட்ட கேட்கணும்னு நினைக்கிறேன்.
context: Suggesting to check with the boss.
explain: 'We should' gives a soft suggestion. 'Before deciding' means first, then decide.
usage: Use it in a team discussion when nobody is sure about a decision.
leelaQ: Who do you ask when you cannot decide something?
answer: I usually ask my elder brother because he gives good advice.

en: Please listen to my idea once before you say no.
tamil: வேண்டாம்னு சொல்றதுக்கு முன்னாடி என் ஐடியாவை ஒரு தடவை கேளுங்க.
context: Asking someone to hear you out.
explain: 'Once' here means 'just one time'. 'Before you say no' makes the request gentle.
usage: Use it with a boss or a parent who may reject your suggestion.
leelaQ: Have you ever convinced someone with a good idea?
answer: Yes, I convinced my father to buy a laptop by explaining my need.

en: My friends are saying that the new mall is crowded.
tamil: புது மால் கூட்டமா இருக்குன்னு என் நண்பர்கள் சொல்லிட்டு இருக்காங்க.
explain: 'Are saying' shares what people say these days.
usage: Use it when you share what others think before making a plan.
leelaQ: What are people saying about your favourite restaurant?
answer: People are saying that it has tasty biryani and quick service.

en: Working from home suits me because I save travel time.
tamil: வீட்டுல இருந்து வேலை செய்றது எனக்கு ஒத்து வருது, ஏன்னா பயண நேரம் மிச்சமாகுது.
context: Giving a reason for liking remote work.
explain: 'Suits me' means something is right for you personally.
usage: Use it in office talks about work from home or hybrid work.
leelaQ: Does working from home suit you, or do you prefer the office?
answer: It suits me because I can start work earlier without any traffic.

en: Will you vote for Ravi in the class election?
tamil: க்ளாஸ் எலக்ஷன்ல நீ ரவிக்கு ஓட்டு போடுவியா?
explain: 'Will you...?' asks about a future decision.
usage: Ask it among classmates or club members before a vote.
leelaQ: Who would be a good class leader, and why?
answer: A good class leader is someone friendly who listens to everyone.

en: It seems to me that the price is quite fair.
tamil: எனக்கு என்னவோ விலை நியாயமா தான் தெரியுது.
context: Giving a careful opinion about price.
explain: 'It seems to me' is a careful, polite way to give an opinion.
usage: Use it when you talk about a price with a seller or a friend.
leelaQ: What do you do when a price seems fair to you?
answer: When a price seems fair, I buy the thing without bargaining much.
